unattested.reason: REFUSED: hard is a defensible opposite of the bare card SMOOTH in a common sense. SMOOTH also means free of difficulty ('it all went smoothly', 'a smooth journey', 'a smooth landing'), and HARD meaning difficult is the sense a 9-11-year-old knows best, so a careful child can argue smooth (easy) / hard (difficult) — and 'a smooth landing / a hard landing' is a real pairing. The row's own twin 'silky' also primes the soft/hard pair. Two defensible opposites on a bare card is a broken row, so this seat may not land even though the door target then falls short.
